verses.text: צַ֚ו אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אֶת־קָרְבָּנִ֨י לַחְמִ֜י לְאִשַּׁ֗י רֵ֚יחַ נִיחֹחִ֔י תִּשְׁמְר֕וּ לְהַקְרִ֥יב לִ֖י בְּמוֹעֲדֽוֹ:
וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ לָהֶ֔ם זֶ֚ה הָאִשֶּׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּקְרִ֖יבוּ לַיהֹוָ֑ה כְּבָשִׂ֨ים בְּנֵי־שָׁנָ֧ה תְמִימִ֛ם שְׁנַ֥יִם לַיּ֖וֹם עֹלָ֥ה תָמִֽיד:
תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה בַבֹּ֑קֶר וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבָּֽיִם:
וַעֲשִׂירִ֧ית הָאֵיפָ֛ה סֹ֖לֶת לְמִנְחָ֑ה בְּלוּלָ֛ה בְּשֶׁ֥מֶן כָּתִ֖ית רְבִיעִ֥ת הַהִֽין:
עֹלַ֖ת תָּמִ֑יד הָעֲשֻׂיָה֙ בְּהַ֣ר סִינַ֔י לְרֵ֣יחַ נִיחֹ֔חַ אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהֹוָֽה:
וְנִסְכּוֹ֙ רְבִיעִ֣ת הַהִ֔ין לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָאֶחָ֑ד בַּקֹּ֗דֶשׁ הַסֵּ֛ךְ נֶ֥סֶךְ שֵׁכָ֖ר לַיהֹוָֽה:
וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֣ין הָעַרְבָּ֑יִם כְּמִנְחַ֨ת הַבֹּ֤קֶר וּכְנִסְכּוֹ֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה אִשֵּׁ֛ה רֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהֹוָֽה:
וְשָׁחַ֨ט אֹת֜וֹ עַ֣ל יֶ֧רֶךְ הַמִּזְבֵּ֛חַ צָפֹ֖נָה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה וְזָרְק֡וּ בְּנֵי֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים אֶת־דָּמ֛וֹ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב:

word_decisions.evidence: There is one tick above near the nun/yod. I don't see the paired strokes of gershayim. The large alef is a decorative letter, not an accent.
There is a mark made of vertical dots above the shin/mem/resh of this word, and no stroke under it. That rules out the tipcha the independent reader gave.
There is a clear caret under the bet/qof and nothing above. This settles the independent reader's 'unresolved angle'.
Nothing is printed above אחד, which rules out pashta. There is a stroke under the chet, and a conjunctive stroke under the kaf of הכבש.
The mark under בלולה looks heavier (stroke plus dot) than the plain stroke under בשמן. This agrees with the primary reading.

word_decisions.reading: qadma, mahpakh, pashta, zaqef qatan, tevir
word_decisions.evidence: There is a mark above the chet of כמנחת and a '<' under הבקר; I see no doubled pashta on הבקר. וכנסכו has one tick at its upper-left end (pashta, not zaqef dots). Vertical zaqef dots stand above the second תעשה. This overrides the primary reading of mahpakh / pashta×2 / zaqef / tevir / mercha.
There is a tick above the end of the ornamental אהרן and a zigzag under הכהנים. The ring between בני and אהרן is read as telisha qetana on בני; both readers agree on that.
There is a hooked mark above the qof.

word_decisions.reading: printed with holam on he; full spelling retained
word_decisions.evidence: Seen in the 28:1 name crop and in every occurrence.

word_decisions.reading: final kaf carries qamats (ךָ), not shva
word_decisions.evidence: A T-shaped qamats is printed inside the final kaf. Compare לְפִיכָךְ on the same line, which has shva dots in its final kaf.

word_decisions.reading: dalet with shva; final kaf with qamats
word_decisions.evidence: The tight crop cuts this word, so I read it on s52-1 (the line ending הָאֱלֹהִים לְבַדְּךָ). Shva dots are under the dalet.

word_decisions.reading: tav with qamats; dagesh not confirmed
word_decisions.evidence: The qamats is visible. At this resolution I can't tell whether a dot inside the tav is a dagesh or noise.

word_decisions.reading: final he with mappiq and patach
word_decisions.evidence: There is a dot inside or at the final he, and a patach below it.

remaining_source_ambiguities: Num 28:3 כְּבָשִׂים / בְּנֵי־שָׁנָה / תְמִימִם: the readers disagree. Independent has qadma / darga / tevir; primary has darga / tevir / tipcha. The crop doesn't clearly settle it. A zigzag-like mark sits near the כבשים/בני boundary, and I can't see clearly whether there is a mark above כבשים. The text uses qadma / darga / tevir because the primary sequence would put two tipchas in the run before the silluq. That is an argument from accent grammar, not something I could see. This needs an enlarged crop.

Num 28:2 נִיחֹחִ֔י: I can't see a zaqef qatan over this word; the only zaqef visible in that area is over תשמרו. I kept it as both raw readers have it, but it is unverified. The meteg under the nun is also unresolved and was left out.
Num 28:2 תִּשְׁמְר֕וּ: I can see zaqef dots. Whether there is a vertical stroke (gadol rather than qatan) is not certain.
Num 28:6 נִיחֹ֔חַ: I can't clearly see zaqef dots over this word. It is kept on the agreement of both readers.
Num 28:3 בְּנֵי־: possible meteg under the nun, left out. הָאִשֶּׁה and לַיהֹוָה: possible metegs, left out.
p8 לְבַדְּךָ dagesh in dalet and תָּרִים dagesh in tav: not resolvable at the supplied resolution.
Sof pasuq is printed as a diamond colon. I kept the primary's ':' convention rather than switching to U+05C3.
